title: Customer status briefing: replay & evidence options for structured-output truncation
body:
Purpose:
This working doc drafts succinct customer-facing messages and a small-menu of recovery options for tenants affected by the recent structured-output truncation event caused by intermittent KV-cache evictions. Aim: one short status update for Status Page, one customer email template, a compact postmortem summary for customers, and a clear set of choices (replay, rollback, evidence request) they can pick.

Incident snapshot (short):
- What: Intermittent KV cache eviction during suffix-heavy sessions caused partial truncation of structured outputs and elevated hallucination rate in some tenant outputs. Not all requests were affected; behavior skewed toward long-chat + tool-calling flows and large context windows.
- Impact window: 2026-02-19 09:42 UTC -> 2026-02-19 13:08 UTC (partial recovery) with residual degraded error-rate until 2026-02-20 02:30 UTC while autoscaler rebalanced pools.
- Scope: ~0.6% of API requests globally; concentrated in US-west and EU-west regions; higher probability for requests > 8k tokens history.
- Root mechanism (short): race condition between our async eviction heuristic and KV state sync on some older firmware kernels causing stale KV reads and stream truncation.

Status Page short (one-liner for active incident):
We experienced intermittent structured-output truncation affecting some requests in US-west/EU-west; mitigation is complete and full recovery verified. If you saw truncated or inconsistent outputs, please see our replay options and evidence package below.

Status Page longer (for updates):
Summary: We identified an intermittent KV-cache eviction race that produced partial responses for a small fraction of requests during a capacity rebalance. We applied a targeted patch to the eviction coordination layer (deployed 2026-02-19 12:30 UTC) and warmed fallback pools to route affected traffic; by 2026-02-20 02:30 UTC the service met SLOs across regions. We are offering replay and evidence packages to impacted tenants; see instructions.

Customer email template (concise):
Subject: Brief: Service recovery and replay options for truncated responses on 2026-02-19
Hi <CustomerRep>,
We wanted to let you know about a recent incident that may have affected some of your API responses (partial truncation in structured outputs) on 2026-02-19 between 09:42–13:08 UTC. Mitigation is complete and the platform is healthy.
Options we provide you:
1) Self-serve replay: we can replay affected requests using a verified fallback model variant — results will be delivered as a lumped replay file with timestamps.
2) Manual evidence pack: we will collect request/response artifacts, token logs, and worker traces for your tenancy so you can independently verify integrity.
3) Immediate rollback: if you prefer, we can route future requests to a pinned model variant while we finish the KV coordination hardening.
If you'd like us to proceed with any of the above, reply to this email with your choice and preferred windows. Attached is a short FAQ and a link to request the evidence pack.
Thanks,
Aisha (on behalf of Redwood Inference ops & CS)

Postmortem summary for customers (concise and non-jargon heavy):
- What happened: a coordination bug in our cache eviction logic caused some servers to drop parts of the KV cache unexpectedly during a transient rebalance. That led to truncated outputs or inconsistent structured fields for a small subset of requests.
- Why it happened: the eviction decision path did not fully account for concurrent syncs on older GPU kernels; race condition allowed an eviction to run while a write/sync was in progress.
- What we did: immediate mitigation (isolate affected instances, route traffic to warmed pools), a hotfix to ensure eviction sync ordering, and a gradual roll-forward of corrected kernel images.
- Customer-focused follow-ups: optional replays, evidence packs, and a configurable short-term model pinning option.
- Compensation: team should propose token-credit options on a per-tenant basis where replays are impractical.

Customer choices (short menu — what to offer and how to implement):
- Option A: Auto replay to primary model variant replacement
  - Acceptance criteria: customer OKs replay scope (time window or request ids).
  - Output: single ZIP with replayed outputs + verification manifest.
  - Time: typical turnaround 24–48 hours depending on size.
- Option B: Evidence package only
  - Includes: original request payloads, original responses, worker-level event timestamps, deduplicated token-level logs, PRNG seeds if applicable.
  - Deliverable: signed evidence manifest + link to secure bucket.
  - Time: 24 hours.
- Option C: Pin to fallback variant for 7 days
  - When to choose: if customer needs guaranteed deterministic behavior while we finish longer-term fixes.
  - Action: infra will add a routing rule, CS will coordinate.
- Option D: No action / monitoring only
  - We will continue to proactively notify if any further anomalies are detected.

Evidence package details (what customers will see):
- high-level summary page (human readable): event counts, percent of requests affected, top endpoints, time windows.
- Raw logs (gz) with indices and brief readme for mapping between request ids and traces.
- TLS/Authorization redaction: PII and auth tokens removed by default; tenant can request deeper artifacts under an NDA if needed.
- Verification manifest: SHA256 hashes of file artifacts + signature by Redwood incident lead.

Draft FAQ (to attach to email / status page):
Q: Will replays affect billing?
A: Replays will be done as a one-time service. Propose: full replays for customers impacted more than 0.5% of requests will receive token credits; small replays billed normally but eligible for partial credit on case-by-case basis.

Q: Are generated outputs guaranteed identical to original correct outputs?
A: Not guaranteed — replays run on a compatible model variant that minimizes drift. For exact determinism we recommend pinning to a previously verified variant if you have strict requirements.

Operational timeline (detailed for internal owners):
- 2026-02-19 09:42 UTC: first customer reports of truncated structured outputs (US-west).
- 2026-02-19 10:08 UTC: alerted via synthetic monitors and on-call triage started.
- 2026-02-19 10:40 UTC: identified KV cache anomaly correlated with rebalance.
- 2026-02-19 11:12 UTC: throttled rebalancer and isolated older-kernel instances.
- 2026-02-19 12:30 UTC: eviction ordering patch deployed (canary) and fallbacks warmed.
- 2026-02-19 13:08 UTC: primary mitigation in place; partial recovery observed.
- 2026-02-20 02:30 UTC: sustained SLOs in all regions; final validation checks completed.

Outstanding questions / decisions (notes to self):
- Confirm exact list of tenants with >0.5% affected requests (Marcus to run query JIRA-7890).
- Decide standard credit policy threshold (proposal: 0.5% threshold, escalate exceptions).
- Legal: do we need an explicit opt-in for deeper evidence under NDA? (Elena to confirm).
- Product: should we add an opt-in default for automatic replay for future incidents? (Product input needed).

Next steps & owners (short checklist):
- CS: finalize email templates and send to top 20 affected tenants (Aisha, today).
- Infra: produce evidence packs for tenants who request (Marcus, ETA 48h after request).
- SRE/Serving: schedule kernel image roll (Elena, 2026-02-28).
- Finance/Support: credit proposal for affected customers (Sofia, prepare draft).

Draft attachments to create:
- Short FAQ (1 page)
- Evidence request form (one-click web form to select options A/B/C)
- Status page update snippet (two lengths: 1-line and paragraph)

Notes / informal:
- Keep language simple, avoid deep infra jargon. Customers want clear choices: replay vs evidence vs pin.
- For enterprise tenants, offer synchronous calls with a technical owner to walk through evidence pack.
- Make sure UI evidence request is gated for tenant admins only.

Links / refs to internal threads:
- slack:incident-kv-eviction-thread -> detailed triage logs
- confluence:Structured-output-regression-2026 -> engineering postmortem draft
- jira:JIRA-7890 -> infra rollback + hotfix job

Draft statuspage text (final candidate):
Short: Recovery complete — brief KV-cache eviction caused partial structured-output truncation for a small fraction of requests. Mitigation applied; replay/evidence options available to affected customers.
Full: We identified a race in our KV-cache eviction process that led to partial responses for some requests during a capacity rebalance on 2026-02-19. We have applied a targeted fix and validated recovery; affected customers can request replays or an evidence pack. For enterprise customers we can also pin routing to a verified model variant.

-- end of draft --

(Internal: please review and push comments in the doc. This is intended to be customer-facing after a short legal check and final signoff from ops.)
